extracted.intended_audience: writers/authors (especially novelists) who want to use TikTok/BookTok to engage readers or promote books
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, platform-specific tips for authors on how to create and share TikTok (BookTok) content that engages readers, builds community, and supports book promotion without prioritising viral fame over craft. Covers content types, etiquette, pitching, and basic production habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have fun
rubrics_metrics.description: This shouldn’t be your reason for creating content [to go viral] — if you feel pressured to be on the app but you don’t want to be, then don’t — it’s a publisher’s job to market you! I love making content on TikTok — it feels like an extension of my creativity...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do BookTok because it excites you: be a bit silly, make entertaining videos, and experiment with pitches. Don’t use assumed virality as your goal. Advice also: better to do one platform well than spread yourself too thin; don’t join if you dislike it. (Anti-pattern: creating content only to chase virality or because you feel pressured.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Spend time on the app
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has particulars you might not pick up on if you don’t spend some time there first. Things like filming in portrait, not leaving a large gap before you begin (tip: use the timer function or cut the clip after you’ve filmed), timing a lip sync to a trending sound—or even working out which sounds are trending—all come from spending time on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn platform norms by consuming content: film in portrait, use timer/cut clips to avoid gaps, time lip-syncs to trending sounds, edit in-app or use CapCut. Engage by commenting and watching others; algorithm rewards dwell time and community interaction. Copy trends if useful but credit originators; repeated jokes/hooks across videos are fine because algorithm shows different viewers. (Examples: use TikTok's editing, watch what performs, comment on other videos.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Why does BookTok interest you? Do you want to... Sell books? Discover the things BookTokers enjoy? Understand your readership better? ... Have a think about why you’re going on the app and let that lead you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set clear objectives (sell, learn, network, research readership, journaling drafting process). Avoid using 'going viral' as the primary metric; focus on what you can control: the content you make. Use your goal to guide content choices and measure success more realistically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t only push your own books
rubrics_metrics.description: The easiest thing to do is make videos where you discuss books — especially if you don’t have a deal yet. Make content about the type of novels you think your readers would enjoy, including your own favorite books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create 'adjacent' content related to your genre or interests (e.g., research trips, reviews, themed content). Example: Bea’s content mix — 70% Greek-myth-based, 25% reviewing/unboxing similar books, 5% demystifying publishing. If you push only your book, you probably won’t grow a following; instead build trust and community with topic-based content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hone your pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: This isn’t what your book is about — it’s why readers will enjoy it. What’s your short snippet? ... You can have a few varied pitches and use them as the basis of your videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop concise reader-focused pitches (one-liners that sell enjoyment/appeal, not detailed plot summaries). Pull out key moments or character hooks to use in videos; imagine convincing a friend to read it. Provide multiple pitch variants for different audiences or angles. (Example pitch provided: 'a sapphic reimagining of the Trojan War featuring rivals to lovers Helen and Cassandra.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes, quotes, quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok loves quotes — though do make sure they end up in the final book! Think of prompts like: ‘The rawest line in fiction...’ ‘The most romantic line...’ ‘No book has ever been so relatable…’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short, striking lines from your work as content; fit them to trending sounds or make carousels with prompts and snippets. Create graphics in Canva or take photos of highlighted quotes. Use prompts to spark engagement. (Tip/anti-pattern: don’t be sneaky with promises like 'FREE BOOKS' to entice viewers.) Ensure any quoted lines are actually in the published book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetics
rubrics_metrics.description: Canva and Pinterest are about to become your new best friends. Videos and images about how your book feels and looks—and its overall vibes—are always popular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce mood/visual content that communicates the book’s vibe: quick image edits, carousels, layered quotes. Use Canva for consistent templates and aesthetic assets. Focus on visual storytelling that matches genre expectations and audience tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrow graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: These are popular across all platforms, and I consider them a sort of landing page or call-to-action for the book. Use a picture of the book with arrows leading out from it to detail the things within—normally tropes, representation, or vibes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use arrow/diagram graphics as bite-sized marketing: show tropes, representation, vibes, or selling points radiating from a cover image. Treat it like a short bullet-point pitch that can end a teaser video or carousel. (Practical tip: end teasers with an arrow graphic to summarise reasons to read.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: Shout about your achievements and cry about the losses — it’s all real, and authenticity is key on TikTok. The moment you sign with a literary agent, get your deal, see your book in stores, receive an email from a reader, hit a list, get nominated for an award... Share it!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about milestones and emotions; sharing wins (and setbacks) builds authenticity and relatability. Use these moments for celebratory content and to motivate followers. (Framing note: it’s aspirational rather than bragging.)

rubrics_metrics.name: People can see you (Be professional / community etiquette)
rubrics_metrics.description: It isn’t just other users and BookTok creators watching your videos. Publishers, agents, other authors—they can all see what you’re posting. So: Don’t be rude. Don’t be mean. Don’t be scathing of other authors or look down on other literature genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional conduct: be considerate, upbeat, and use your platform to lift others up. Avoid harsh reviewer/author role conflicts; don’t intrude into reviewer spaces if you’re an author without treading a fine balance. Remember industry professionals are watching—avoid public feuds and nastiness.
